title: Processing preserves free variables in the base restriction
statement: Fix a number $n$ of variables. Let $\mathrm{lits}$ be a list of literals, each paired with its position index in a clause; let $\mathrm{path}$ be a decision-tree path; let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on the $n$ variables; and let $v$ be a variable. Let $\rho_0'$ denote the updated restriction produced in place of $\rho_0$ by the clause-processing procedure applied to $\mathrm{lits}$, $\mathrm{path}$, $\rho_0$, and $\sigma$. If $\rho_0'$ leaves $v$ free, then $\rho_0$ already leaves $v$ free.
hypotheses_covered: a literal-and-index list, a path, restrictions rho_0 and sigma, and a variable v
the updated rho_0 restriction produced by the clause-processing procedure is free (none) at v
replaced:
If the restriction component $(\mathrm{processClauseLits}\ \mathit{lits}\ \mathit{path}\ \rho_0\ \sigma).2.1$
is unset at a variable $v$ (equal to \texttt{none}), then $\rho_0$ is already unset at $v$,
i.e.\ $\rho_0\,v = \texttt{none}$.
